Delivery Hero treats the pre-August 2021 Spanish model as probable and provisioned for it, while the post-August 2021 model is treated as a possible (not probable) contingency disclosed in the notes. Glovo decided to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain from 2025.

- For the model operated until August 2021, the risk is "more likely than not" to materialize, so appropriate provisions are reflected in the Consolidated Financial Statements; Glovo also had to provide bank guarantees to Spanish courts in 2024 to secure claimed liabilities [4], [3].
- For the model in place since August 2021, the risk is deemed possible but not probable, so it is disclosed as a contingency of € 440.0 to 770.0 million (social security contributions, late payment charges, fines, and possible VAT claims), with no provision recognized since court reclassification was assessed as not probable [4], [5], [2].
- In December 2024, Glovo's management decided to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain (effective 2025) to avoid further legal uncertainties, though Glovo will still defend the self-employed status through all available instances for the ongoing investigations [1], [6], [8].

Zalando - end of 2022: EUR 304.3m committed to invest in fulfilment centres
Zalando - end of 2024: 59.5m EUR committed to invest in fulfilment centres

The commitment fell from EUR 304.3m at the end of 2022 to 59.5m EUR at the end of 2024, a decrease of 244.8m EUR (304.3 − 59.5).
Approximately 850,000 riders delivered at least one order for Delivery Hero in 2024.

In 2024, Zalando evolved Zalando Plus from a paid membership to a free-to-join model, introducing a points-based system that rewards customer loyalty for purchases and other engagement activities (e.g., subscribing to newsletters), with points unlocking four benefit levels; it was initially tested in Spain and expanded to France and Austria, with further rollout planned for 2025 [1][4][6]. The awards create a separate performance obligation providing a material right to customers [2]. At year-end 2024, the report mentions increased accruals for the reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025, included in "others" within other current non-financial liabilities (which rose to 377.4m EUR) [3][9][10].

Turkcell - 2G licence extension (April 2023): EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes); paid in installments — an initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (down payment plus VAT) paid in Turkish Lira at TRY 1.7 billion during 2023, approximately half of the remaining installments (EUR 31.1 million) paid in April 2024 in Turkish Lira at TRY 1.1 billion, with the remaining amount to be paid within a year.
Vodafone Turkey - 2G licence extension (900 MHz): €120 million for a six-year extension until 30 April 2029 (excluding 18% VAT); paid the extension fee in advance with a capital injection and signed the extension agreement effective as of 27 April 2023.

Both operators agreed to the same headline extension fee of EUR/EURO 120 million (excluding VAT), but they paid it differently: Vodafone Turkey paid the fee in advance via a capital injection, while Turkcell paid in installments in Turkish Lira, with part of the fee still outstanding.
